transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-05-23 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Kim; Samira Patel; Marco Ruiz; Daniel Ortiz; Priya Menon; Liam O'Connor; Esha Rao

Auto-generated summary (brief):
Redwood and CobaltBridge discussed an initial integration pattern for a SaaS connector to offload inference for their multi-tenant analytics platform. Key topics: tenant isolation, routing policies (hosted vs dedicated), security controls (KMS, SSO), and pilot scope (throughput and SLA). Next: security deep-dive and pilot plan.

Topics:
- Multi-tenant connector architecture
- Dedicated capacity for batch transforms vs hosted low-latency endpoints
- Data residency, encryption, and audit logs
- Pilot framing and benchmarks

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone thanks for joining on a Friday, appreciate the time. Quick round-robin, i'm Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE here. Samira is our SE and Marco's on for architecture.
[00:12] Daniel Ortiz: Hi Alex, Daniel here. Thanks, excited to talk about how we can offload some of our embedding and rerank jobs to something managed.
[00:18] Priya Menon: Priya here. We're evaluating latency and cost tradeoffs, primarily.
[00:22] Samira Patel: Nice to meet you all. I'll try to keep notes on topology options. Quick question up-front — what are your top requirements for the connector?
[00:31] Daniel Ortiz: Good question. Number one: tenant isolation. We can't have data cross-tenant. Number two: predictable costs — we run large nightly batches that spike. Third: security and audit — SOC2 and KMS are mandatory.
[00:45] Alex Kim: Got it. That's very typical. For tenant isolation we usually surface two patterns: a hosted per-tenant keying and logical isolation, or Dedicated Pools where you can isolate at capacity level. Both can be combined with VPC peering for Private deployments.
[01:07] Esha Rao: quick clarification — by Dedicated Pools do you mean reserved GPU capacity in Redwood Dedicated? Is that separate infra or a config?
[01:13] Marco Ruiz: yes, it’s reserved capacity. Basically you can reserve a set of nodes that only your traffic routes to. It’s about throughput predictability and tenancy isolation.
[01:22] Priya Menon: What's the cost delta roughly between hosted and dedicated for batch peeks? ballpark numbers?
[01:29] Alex Kim: Ballpark — hosted per-token is lower up to moderate qps, but when you have sustained high throughput dedicated can be 30-60% cheaper per token because of fixed capacity and better packing/batching. There's an operational overhead too — Dedicated requires commit and some configuration. We'll share a one-pager.
[01:46] Liam O'Connor: Security — we use HashiCorp Vault for keys and AWS KMS in some regions. Need to understand KMS integrations and whether Redwood can integrate with external HSM/KMS and support tenant-specific keys.
[01:58] Samira Patel: We do support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and have integrations for SSM/Vault patterns in Dedicated workflows. For hosted we support envelope encryption and bring-your-own-key in certain enterprise tiers. We'll put together the exact flow for KMS handshake and token scoping.
[02:16] Daniel Ortiz: Nice. Audit logs — we need per-request logs for compliance, and retention of 12 months. Do you store logs in the customer account or do we pull them?
[02:25] Marco Ruiz: We offer log streaming to customer sinks (S3/GCS) or via SIEM connectors. Retention and export are configurable. For Private deployments logs remain in your VPC.
[02:36] Priya Menon: Ok, on the integration surface — we call out to inference for embeddings and rerank. We have a bunch of legacy endpoints that expect sync < 300ms p95. For embeddings it's more tolerant. How do you recommend pathing those?
[02:48] Samira Patel: Typical approach: keep low-latency calls on hosted endpoints pinned to smaller models or quantized variants with autoscale. For bulk batch transforms, push to Dedicated pool with large batch sizes and async endpoints. Also caching prefixes can shave a lot off for repeated prompts.
[03:06] Daniel Ortiz: Could you explain KV cache and prefix caching a bit? sounds like it could help our rerank jobs.
[03:11] Marco Ruiz: Sure. KV cache is the cached key/value attention state for long-running contexts. Prefix caching is storing common request prefixes — if you hit the same prompt prefix we can cache embeddings or intermediate KV states which avoids recomputation. It's workload dependent.
[03:25] Esha Rao: Our nightly job is mostly rerank over 100M items — we'll stream features, run batch embedding and a rerank. Latency not critical there but throughput and cost are.
[03:36] Alex Kim: Great use-case for Dedicated. We can tune batching to hit high GPU utilization and recommend quantization profiles per model family.
[03:44] Priya Menon: Any constraints around model versions? we need deterministic outputs for A/B tests.
[03:49] Samira Patel: You can pin model versions for serving and do canary rollouts. Redwood Optimize will also surface regressions if outputs deviate on eval prompts.
[03:59] Liam O'Connor: On the compliance front — do you support SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, role-based access controls? We need to map roles to our internal teams and log admin actions.
[04:10] Alex Kim: Yes — enterprise tiers support SSO via SAML/OIDC, SCIM, fine-grained RBAC, and detailed audit logs. We'll include our product doc links in the follow-up.
[04:20] Daniel Ortiz: Cool — what about network egress and data residency? Some of our EU customers require inference to remain in eu-west regions.
[04:28] Marco Ruiz: We can route by region with Smart Routing and enforce region pins. For strict residency you'd use Private deployment in the region or dedicate a region in Dedicated pool.
[04:39] Priya Menon: For the pilot, we're thinking 3 months, proof points: 1) integrate connector with our onboarding pipeline, 2) run a 24h stress test to 5k qps of batch requests, 3) validate SSO/KMS and logs. Is that reasonable?
[04:54] Samira Patel: Yes that's a solid pilot. We'll propose a topology: small Dedicated pool for batch jobs + hosted endpoints for low-latency endpoints, with routing rules and a toggle for processing mode.
[05:06] Alex Kim: On commercial terms — we can do a pilot discount and a credit to run benchmarks. For enterprise deals we'll map committed capacity. We'll send sample pricing and a dedicated vs hosted TCO comparison.
[05:20] Liam O'Connor: One blocker could be our legal/compliance review — we need a vendor security pack and the SOC2 attestation.
[05:28] Alex Kim: We'll attach the security pack in the follow-up. Also we can set up a separate call with our compliance specialist if needed.
[05:36] Daniel Ortiz: Great. Any concerns about multi-tenant noisy neighbors? our tenants vary widely in size.
[05:43] Marco Ruiz: It's something we mitigate via routing policies and auto-fallback to spare capacity. For critical tenants you can assign dedicated slices or assign priority routing.
[05:54] Esha Rao: For the webhook/ingest side — do you provide backpressure signals or retry semantics? we need idempotency guarantees.
[06:02] Samira Patel: We expose async job endpoints with status polling, webhooks with retry/backoff and idempotency keys. We'll share the connector spec.
[06:12] Priya Menon: that sounds good. who will own the dev work on our side? we'll likely assign two engineers and a PM. Our timeline is wanting a pilot kickoff by mid-June.
[06:23] Alex Kim: Sounds achievable. We'll have Samira draft a pilot plan with milestones and a requirements list for the infra team.
[06:30] Daniel Ortiz: Last quick item — competitors. we evaluated NeuronGrid and CloudApex. NeuronGrid had a tighter pricing for bursty spikes but integration friction; CloudApex had better SLAs. curious how Redwood differentiates on ops and observability.
[06:44] Samira Patel: We focus on production-grade observability: token-level costs, per-route dashboards, tracing hooks, and regression alerts tied to eval prompts. Also unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private reduces surprises at cutover.
[06:58] Alex Kim: to recap next steps: Alex sends security and pricing info; Samira drafts pilot and perf questions; Liam will share KMS/compliance details; schedule follow-up technical deep dive next week.
[07:12] Priya Menon: ok thanks all, this was productive.
[07:16] Alex Kim: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links and calendar invites.

End of transcript.
